heading: Native Go packages
body:
A Go app often has its own packages: a git client, a JSON schema checker, a repository layer. These are plain Go packages, not Tachyon roles. Put them in `server/packages/`. This folder holds one Go module. `server/packages/go.mod` names the module, and each folder under it is a normal Go package with its own package name. Controllers, services and other role files import a package with the module path, for example `import "example.com/shop/packages/pricing"`. The packages can import each other the same way. A route can take or return a type from these packages, such as `spec.Document`. Tachyon reads fields only from `server/models/`, so such a type is an open JSON value that Go's `encoding/json` reads and writes.

Tachyon does not treat code in `server/packages/` as roles. It is like a library on the Spring classpath: it is not a bean, because nothing registers it. So these files need no role marker, and the role folder, file name, one-class, cohesion, duplicate and visibility rules do not apply to them. The secret and code safety checks still run, except in `vendor/`. Tachyon builds every Go handler inside this module, in a folder of its own, so the import works with no download. Handler code is therefore compiled with the Go version that the module's `go` line names.

The folder has a few limits. `server/packages/go.mod` may hold only `module`, `go`, `toolchain` and `require` lines. A required third-party module must be vendored, as the next section shows. A second `go.mod` inside the folder is refused. Go code there cannot carry a Tachyon annotation, because an annotated type belongs in its role folder. Other Yon languages' source files are refused there. The folder `server/packages/yonhandler/` is reserved, because Tachyon builds each handler program there. Other files, such as JSON schemas for `go:embed`, are allowed. Each of these mistakes fails with `TY1310`. A Go file in `server/packages/` without `server/packages/go.mod` also fails with `TY1310`.

Use the folder for code that is not a role. A type with a role marker stays in its role folder, such as `server/services/`. A plain helper of package main can stay in `server/shared/`. When `TY1363` reports a Go file in a role folder without its marker, decide what it is: mark a real role, or move a native package to `server/packages/` (ADR 0095).

The folder is for Go only, so this section has one language. JavaScript, TypeScript, Python, PHP, Java, Groovy, Kotlin, C#, F#, Rust, Dart, Ruby, Lua and C++ keep their own module rules (see Application modules), and their source files in `server/packages/` fail with `TY1310`.
